reviews.title: SQL query built from user-controlled sources
reviews.explanation: The endpoint `catalog_search` constructs an SQL statement by directly interpolating the user‑supplied query parameter `q` into the query string using an f‑string. This results in a classic SQL injection vector because the value of `q` is not sanitized or passed as a parameter to the database driver. An attacker can supply crafted input (e.g., `q=%'; DROP TABLE products;--`) that will be executed by the database.
reviews.impact: An attacker could execute arbitrary SQL commands, leading to data leakage, data modification, or complete compromise of the database. This may allow reading sensitive product information, deleting or altering records, or escalating privileges within the application.
reviews.remediation: Replace the string interpolation with a parameterized query using the database library's placeholder syntax (e.g., `conn.execute("SELECT name FROM products WHERE name ILIKE %s", (f"%{q}%",))`).
